definition: Singular value decomposition is a factorization of a real or complex matrix that generalizes the eigendecomposition of a square normal matrix to any \(m \times n\) matrix via an extension of the polar decomposition.
details: Singular value decomposition is a factorization of a real or complex matrix that generalizes the eigendecomposition of a square normal matrix to any \(m \times n\) matrix via an extension of the polar decomposition.

explainer.lead: SVD factorizes any real or complex matrix, generalizing eigendecomposition beyond square normal matrices to any m-by-n matrix. It matters as a foundational tool for decomposing rectangular data.

tiers.eli5: It's a way of splitting any grid of numbers into simpler building blocks, even when the grid isn't square.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply SVD to factor matrices of any shape; a pitfall is expecting eigendecomposition-style behavior, since SVD generalizes it via an extension of the polar decomposition and applies to non-square, non-normal cases.
tiers.paperLevel: A factorization of a real or complex matrix generalizing the eigendecomposition of a square normal matrix to any m × n matrix via an extension of the polar decomposition.

explainer.example: Factorizing an m-by-n data matrix that is neither square nor normal, which eigendecomposition alone could not handle.
